observations.text: SP flew the localizer-only final approach with the IP directing the timing from the FAF and setting the computed final approach airspeed for the descent. Localizer displacement reached 2.4 dots and the aircraft was leveled at MDA only after the IP flew part of the level-off. Performance was at the desired code for this Training Section but marginal; independent timing from the FAF and an earlier CDI cross-check after the fix are expected to improve.

SP, following the IP's verbal prompts on the CDI and on the MDA level-off, completed the localizer final approach without IP intervention on the controls. Localizer displacement peaked at 2 dots and the aircraft was held 200 feet above MDA before the descent was continued, with both deviations recognized and corrected with delay. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, maintaining a cross-check between the CDI and the altimeter, tracked the localizer final approach course and leveled at MDA without IP prompts. Localizer displacement did not exceed 1.5 dots, MDA was captured 150 feet high and the computed final approach airspeed was flown 12 knots fast, with each error recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP complied with ATC instructions, respected the published step-down altitude restrictions and flew the localizer-only descent to MDA with accuracy and speed. Localizer displacement remained within 0.6 dot, MDA was maintained within 60 feet high with no descent below it, and the computed final approach airspeed was held within 5 knots. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the localizer-only approach with an uninterrupted instrument cross-check, timing started exactly at the FAF and the landing configuration set before the descent. Deviations were negligible, with localizer displacement within 0.2 dot, MDA held within 20 feet high and airspeed within 2 knots of the computed final approach airspeed to the missed approach point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect drift correction applied to the localizer final approach course, did not stop the CDI displacement and did not level the aircraft at MDA. The result was a localizer displacement of 2.6 dots and a descent 80 feet below MDA, with the IP directing the level-off and flying part of the re-intercept of the final approach course. Further study of the localizer-only approach technique is required.

SP, due to poor workload distribution, with navigation, communication and aircraft control attempted simultaneously, did not monitor the CDI after the FAF and did not set the computed final approach airspeed for the descent. The result was a localizer displacement of 2.5 dots and an airspeed 18 knots below the computed final approach airspeed, corrected only after the IP took the aircraft and re-established the final approach course.

SP completed the localizer final approach at the desired code for this Training Section, with localizer displacement held at 2 dots and MDA captured 200 feet high before the descent was continued. Both deviations were recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts and with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section - an earlier, unprompted CDI cross-check after the FAF is expected to improve.

SP, applying a stable drift correction after the FAF, tracked the localizer final approach course and leveled at MDA without IP intervention. Localizer displacement did not exceed 1.5 dots, MDA was reached 140 feet high and the computed final approach airspeed was flown 12 knots fast, with each error recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP set the landing configuration before the FAF, started the timing at the fix and flew the localizer-only descent to MDA with accuracy and speed. Localizer displacement remained within 0.8 dot, MDA was maintained within 70 feet high with no descent below it, and airspeed stayed within 6 knots of the computed final approach airspeed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the localizer final approach in accordance with the standardized procedure, complied with all ATC instructions and respected every published altitude restriction. Deviations were negligible, with localizer displacement within 0.2 dot, MDA held within 20 feet high and airspeed within 3 knots of the computed final approach airspeed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to over-controlling in the corrections to the localizer final approach course, did not stabilize the CDI after the FAF and did not arrest the descent at MDA. The result was a localizer displacement of 2.8 dots and a descent 100 feet below MDA, with the IP directing the level-off and flying part of the re-intercept of the final approach course. Further study of the localizer-only approach technique is required.

SP, due to an undesired aircraft state that was allowed to persist rather than being corrected, did not re-intercept the localizer final approach course and did not maintain the computed final approach airspeed after the FAF. The result was a localizer displacement of 3 dots and an airspeed 20 knots fast at MDA, with the IP taking the aircraft and directing the missed approach.

SP, due to a late start of the timing from the FAF, did not begin the descent at the correct point and did not complete the level-off at MDA within the published segment. MDA was captured 200 feet high and localizer displacement was held at 2 dots, with recognition and correction following the IP's verbal prompts and completed with delay.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established on final, did not maintain the instrument cross-check on the CDI and did not hold the computed final approach airspeed. Localizer displacement reached 2 dots and airspeed decayed to 10 knots below the computed final approach airspeed; both were recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts and with delay.

SP flew the localizer final approach within the desired standards; however, localizer displacement twice reached 1.6 dots and MDA was captured 150 feet high before the descent to the missed approach point was continued. All deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without IP intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a tighter drift correction after the FAF and earlier anticipation of the MDA level-off are expected to improve.

SP complied with ATC instructions, respected the published routing and altitude restrictions and flew the localizer-only descent to MDA with accuracy and speed. Localizer displacement remained within 0.7 dot, MDA was maintained within 60 feet high with no descent below it, and the computed final approach airspeed was held within 5 knots to the missed approach point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP briefed and flew the localizer final approach without a single prompt, with the landing configuration and the timing complete before the FAF. Deviations were negligible, with localizer displacement within 0.2 dot, MDA held within 20 feet high and airspeed within 2 knots of the computed final approach airspeed. The missed approach was initiated without hesitation at the computed missed approach point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to failure to identify and monitor the localizer facility before the final approach segment, did not track the final approach course and did not respect the published step-down altitude restrictions. The result was a localizer displacement of 3 dots and an altitude 120 feet below the step-down minimum, with the IP directing the re-intercept and flying part of the approach. Further study of the localizer-only approach procedure is required.

SP, due to an incorrect assumption about which navigation mode was active, did not select the localizer as the primary course reference and did not detect the resulting displacement from the final approach course. The result was a localizer displacement beyond 3 dots at the final approach fix, with the IP taking the aircraft, correcting the navigation source and directing the re-intercept.

SP, due to an inadequate power reduction at the FAF, did not establish the computed final approach airspeed for the descent and did not achieve the descent rate required to reach MDA in the published segment. Airspeed reached 15 knots above the computed final approach airspeed and MDA was captured 200 feet high, with recognition and correction achieved only after the IP's verbal prompts and completed with delay.

SP, due to a degraded basic instrument scan after prolonged automated navigation, did not hold the localizer final approach course within the required displacement and did not level the aircraft at MDA on the first attempt. Localizer displacement reached 2 dots and MDA was captured 190 feet high; both deviations were recognized and corrected after the IP's verbal prompts and with delay.

SP, due to a delayed drift correction after the FAF, did not keep the localizer final approach course centered and allowed the CDI to displace before applying a heading change. Localizer displacement reached 1.5 dots and MDA was captured 140 feet high, with both deviations recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without IP intervention.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase, did not complete the landing configuration before the FAF and did not stabilize the computed final approach airspeed at the start of the descent. Airspeed was flown 12 knots fast and localizer displacement reached 1.4 dots, with both deviations recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without IP intervention.

SP flew the localizer final approach at the desired code for this Training Section, complying with ATC instructions and with the published routing and altitude restrictions. Localizer displacement remained within 1 dot and MDA was held within 100 feet high with no descent below it, although both values sat at the upper end of the tolerance on the second approach. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a finer drift correction after the FAF and earlier anticipation of the MDA level-off are expected to improve.

SP flew the localizer-only approach with an uninterrupted instrument cross-check, exact timing from the FAF and the missed approach initiated precisely at the missed approach point. Deviations were negligible, with localizer displacement within 0.2 dot, MDA maintained within 20 feet high and airspeed within 2 knots of the computed final approach airspeed. Above end of block MIF achieved.
